title: Agent Observability: Langfuse, Phoenix, Opik
service: TraceJudge: a stdlib agent-observability backend with retry-safe span ingest, the lesson's scripted LLM judge per trace, a SQLite annotation queue, prompt-version regression bisection, batch ingestion of out-of-order span events pushed as SSE, and trace clustering by span-tree signature
runtime: Python 3.10+, standard library, pytest; no network and no LLM: the judge is the lesson's scripted rubric

parts.lesson_anchor: Build It: ingest GenAI-shaped spans, group by session, scripted LLM judge, dashboard summary; code/main.py TraceCollector, scripted_llm_judge, summarize
planted_bugs: load_spans keeps "tokens": "800" as a string although its docstring promises an int; the TypeError surfaces three calls later in scripted_llm_judge, and coercing only in the judge moves it to the token sum
TraceCollector.ingest does not dedupe, so a span the exporter retried is counted twice (errors, tokens, span count)
trace_count is len(spans), as in the lesson's code
eval_score_mean judges the whole session as one trace, as in the lesson's code, instead of judging each trace and averaging
summarize calls by_session() once per session, regrouping every span each time: O(sessions x spans)
parts.timing_assert: two asserts, measured on this machine (Apple M5, Python 3.12, other agents running, load 8 to 11). A whole batch of 8000 spans resent once must ingest under 0.05 s: reference 1.2-3 ms (7 ms at worst under load), a dedupe that scans the stored spans 1.2 s, keys kept in a list 0.43-0.48 s. 5000 one-span sessions ingested and summarized under 0.15 s: quadratic version 1.9 s (3.4 s under heavy load), fixed version 11-14 ms (up to 39 ms under load 11)
parts.overfix_guard: two chat spans in one trace stay separate (rules out deduping on trace_id and name); span ids 1, 2, 3 repeat in every trace of sess-b (rules out deduping on span_id alone); load_spans is checked directly, so coercing tokens in the judge and the sum instead fails; a scan- or list-based dedupe fails the resend timing assert

parts.lesson_anchor: Langfuse: annotation queues and user feedback (open-sourced under MIT in June 2025)
parts.exactness: annotations round-trip exactly across close and reopen: a 19-digit created_ns, a score of 0.0 next to a missing score, 1/3 and 0.1 + 0.2, notes with newlines, CRLF and leading spaces
traps: created_ns in a REAL column loses the last digits
score or None turns 0.0 into None
ORDER BY created_ns instead of recording order (annotator clocks drift)
INSERT OR REPLACE moves a re-queued trace to the back
pending sorted by trace id (tr-10 before tr-9)
NaN and out-of-range scores rejected without writing anything

parts.lesson_anchor: Where this pattern goes wrong: prompt versions not tied to traces, so you cannot bisect to the prompt that caused a regression; Key Terms: prompt management, versioned prompts tied to traces
traps: versions sorted as strings (v1.10 before v1.9), or compared as floats
WARN counted as a pass
each version compared with the previous one, so a slow drift never trips
the drop compared in floats: 68% - 58% is 0.10000000000000009; percentages computed first are exact there, so 9/14 against 19/35 is tested too
the drop or the pass rates rounded to whole points: 10/11 against 21/26 drops 10.14 points
a drop of exactly max_drop counted as a regression
inconclusive versions (fewer than min_traces) blamed, or a version with exactly min_traces treated as inconclusive
versions older than known_good scanned, or versions walked in arrival order
suspects missing the inconclusive versions between last_good and the culprit, or collected since known_good
parts.integration: none; the pairs are (prompt_version, verdict) as the Part 1 judge would produce them

parts.lesson_anchor: The Problem: the platform ingests spans; Key Terms: tracing (ingest spans, index by session); the lesson's summary per session, updated live
parts.wire_format: SSE: id, event and data lines and a blank line per event, one event per yielded string; session events carry the SessionSummary as JSON, dropped events carry {"updates": n}; parsed by the test the way EventSource does
traps: updates applied in arrival order instead of latest ts per field
one ts per span instead of per field, or update attributes replacing the stored ones
an update that arrives before its create is lost
a waiting update older than its create overriding the create's values
orphan TTL off by one batch, in either direction
updates still waiting at the end of the stream not reported
an event for a session that was touched but did not change
session events in the order sessions were touched instead of session_id order
a retried create resetting an updated span
every batch read before anything is written (probe counts pulled batches)
ids restarting per batch

parts.lesson_anchor: Arize Phoenix: trace clustering and anomaly detection; Key Terms: trace clustering (cluster similar runs for drift detection)
traps: children in input order, by span_id alone, or by start_ns without the span_id tie-break
roots in input order
span ids resolved across traces
a span whose parent is missing not treated as a root
names not escaped, so chat(retry) collides with chat > retry; the backslash escaped after the brackets
a share of exactly min_share flagged
the share taken over the number of clusters instead of the number of traces
trace ids sorted inside a cluster instead of kept in first-seen order
spans on a parent cycle (including a self-parent) silently left out

deviations: Part 1: the three suggested defects are kept (retry dedupe on (trace_id, span_id), per-trace judging averaged over the session, string tokens failing in the judge). trace_count = len(spans), also straight from the lesson's code, is a fourth layer. The suggested 'two chats in one trace' guard is kept, and a second guard, span ids repeating across traces, rules out deduping on span_id alone. The timing case is 5000 one-span sessions so the quadratic version stays near two seconds; a second timing case resends a whole batch of 8000 spans, because a scanning dedupe is only about twice as slow as the limit on the first case.

Part 1: the lesson's Span has no span_id, parent_id or start_ns; the exam's Span adds them (Part 5 needs the tree). The span names, the gen_ai.output.reference_id, gen_ai.tool.name, error.reason and tokens attributes and the judge's rubric are the lesson's.

Part 2: SQLite as assigned. Missing commit is not a designed trap because chapter 14 already uses it more than twice. The designed exactness trap is a 19-digit created_ns in a REAL column, next to 0.0 versus None for the score. Re-annotation by the same person keeps both rows instead of replacing, so the queue has one INSERT OR REPLACE trap only.

Part 3: the threshold is an integer number of percentage points so that 'exactly max_drop' has an exact meaning; the bisection compares every version with the known-good rate, and 'last good' names the start of the suspect range rather than a moving baseline. The verdict pairs are given directly instead of being read from span attributes, because the lesson names no attribute for the prompt version.

Part 4: SSE as assigned. The create/update event shape is this exam's own convention, not a Langfuse or OTel format. Per-field last-writer-wins by ts replaces the suggested per-span merge so that two updates touching different fields are both kept. Session events are written in session_id order after each batch, and a dropped count follows them.

Part 5: as suggested, except that repeated chat spans are simply kept (a clarifying question) instead of being a trap, and parent cycles were added because a top-down walk silently leaves those spans out.
